n: Prince Mohammed bin Salman Royal Reserve
na: محمية الأمير محمد بن سلمان الملكية
s: Royal reserve from the Hejaz Mountains to the Red Sea coast · onagers roaming free again
dr: Royal reserve by royal decree, June 2018; WDPA 555785931
te: Where wild asses run free again
ta: حيث تعدو الحمير البرية من جديد
se: A vast royal reserve between NEOM, the Red Sea Project and AlUla, where wild asses run free for the first time in over 100 years
sa: محمية ملكية شاسعة بين نيوم ومشروع البحر الأحمر والعُلا، تعدو فيها الحمير البرية طليقة لأول مرة منذ أكثر من 100 عام
desc: Established by royal decree in June 2018, the reserve covers about 24,500 km² of north-western Saudi Arabia across parts of Tabuk and Madinah provinces, between NEOM, the Red Sea Project and AlUla. It takes in about 1% of the Kingdom's land and 1.8% of its territorial waters, with 15 ecosystems from the Hejaz Mountains to the Red Sea coast. Persian onagers have been released as a stand-in for the extinct Syrian wild ass, the first free-running wild asses in Saudi Arabia in over 100 years, alongside reintroduced Arabian oryx and gazelles. The World Database on Protected Areas records 24,485 km².
sig: One of the largest rewilding landscapes in Arabia, joining mountain, desert and Red Sea habitats under one royal reserve.
refs: Wikipedia. Prince Mohammad bin Salman Royal Reserve. https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Prince_Mohammad_bin_Salman_Royal_Reserve

s: Traditional protected rangeland in the sands near Unaizah · named for the ghada shrub
te: The hima of the ghada sands
se: A protected rangeland of sand near Unaizah in Al-Qassim, named after the ghada shrub and covering about 1,000 km²
sa: مرعى محمي من الرمال قرب عنيزة في القصيم، يحمل اسم شجيرة الغضا وتبلغ مساحته نحو 1,000 كم²
desc: A hima, a traditionally protected rangeland, in Al-Qassim Region, recorded in the World Database on Protected Areas with 1,011 km². Arabic Wikipedia's list of protected areas classes it as a hima/recreation area and gives 1,186.22 km². The National Center for Vegetation Cover names the Al-Ghadha Reserve as a landmark beside Unaizah National Park, which lies about 7 km from Unaizah city. The name refers to the ghada, or white saxaul (Haloxylon persicum), a desert shrub.
sig: One of Saudi Arabia's traditional himas, protecting the ghada sand country around Unaizah.

s: Tuwaiq valley park with seasonal springs · among the Kingdom's first Green Flag Award parks
dr: National park, 2001 (Arabic Wikipedia list); WDPA 555624838; Green Flag Award, February 2024
se: A park of two valleys in the Tuwaiq Mountains, with springs that flow in the wet season and newborn reem gazelles
sa: منتزه يضم واديين في جبال طويق، تجري ينابيعه في موسم الأمطار وتولد فيه صغار غزال الريم
desc: A national park near Al-Ghat in Riyadh Region, listed with an area of 58.67 km² and a 2001 designation in Arabic Wikipedia's list of protected areas. It lies in the Tuwaiq Mountains and takes in two valleys formerly known locally as Wadi Al-Batin, with natural springs at each end that flow in the wet season. Managed by the National Center for Vegetation Cover Development and Combating Desertification, it was one of the first two parks in Saudi Arabia to receive a Green Flag Award, in February 2024. Ten reem gazelles were born in the park in April 2025.
sig: A restored Tuwaiq valley landscape that set the first international park-management benchmark in Saudi Arabia.

s: Tuwaiq wadi park near Huraymila · tree felling banned by royal decree
te: A green wadi in the Tuwaiq hills
se: A wadi about 100 km from Riyadh, ringed by the Tuwaiq Mountains, where acacia trees and desert plants are protected
sa: وادٍ على بُعد نحو 100 كم من الرياض تحيط به جبال طويق، تُحمى فيه أشجار الطلح والنباتات الصحراوية
desc: A national park near Huraymila in Riyadh Region, listed with 147.32 km² in Arabic Wikipedia's list of protected areas and recorded in the WDPA (ID 28810). A botanical account describes the Huraymila protected area as a wadi about 100 km from Riyadh, surrounded by the Tuwaiq Mountains at about 810 m altitude. Acacia gerrardii, Lycium shawii and Rhazya stricta dominate the wadis, while Rhanterium epapposum and Zygophyllum migahidii grow on plateaus and hilltops. Tree felling is prohibited by royal decree; controlled grazing and picnicking are allowed.
sig: A protected Tuwaiq wadi that keeps a sample of central Najd vegetation close to Riyadh.
ex: Plant Diversity of Saudi Arabia; Protected Planet
disc: Tree felling banned by royal decree

s: Sandstone and dune reserve on the western Nafud · stronghold of the reem gazelle
dr: Natural reserve 1987; grouped into King Salman bin Abdulaziz Royal Reserve, June 2018
te: Gazelle country on the Nafud's edge
se: A huge reserve north of Tayma on the edge of the Nafud, home to reem gazelles, houbara and lappet-faced vultures
sa: محمية شاسعة شمال تيماء على حافة النفود، موطن لغزال الريم والحبارى والنسر الأذون
desc: Designated a natural reserve in 1987, Al-Khunfah covers 19,339 km² on the western edge of the Nafud desert north of Tayma, in Tabuk Region. Its terrain is mostly sandstone, with mountains reaching 1,141 m, plateaus, wadis and sand dunes, and plants including acacia, ghada and tamarisk. The reem gazelle is its main species, with a small number of addax, and birds include houbara bustards, sandgrouse and lappet-faced vultures. In June 2018 it was grouped with At-Tubayq and Harrat al-Harrah as the King Salman bin Abdulaziz Royal Reserve.
sig: One of Saudi Arabia's oldest large reserves, safeguarding the gazelles and raptors of the Nafud fringe.
disc: Now in King Salman Royal Reserve

s: Rugged dark-rock reserve on the Jordan border · Nubian ibex, gazelles and wolves
dr: Natural reserve 1989; now part of King Salman bin Abdulaziz Royal Reserve
te: The dark mountains of the ibex
se: A reserve of dark, rugged rock in the far north-west, where Nubian ibex, gazelles and wolves roam
sa: محمية من الصخور الداكنة الوعرة في أقصى الشمال الغربي، تجوب فيها الوعول النوبية والغزلان والذئاب
desc: Designated a natural reserve in 1989, At-Tubayq covers 12,105 km² of north-western Saudi Arabia along the border with Jordan, a landscape of dark, rugged rock named after Jabal at-Tubayq. Mammals recorded include Nubian ibex, gazelles, wolves, foxes and hares, with falcons, partridges and eagles among the birds. In June 2018 it was grouped with Al-Khunfah and Harrat al-Harrah as the King Salman bin Abdulaziz Royal Reserve. The map point is Jabal at-Tubayq peak, at 1,082 m.
sig: Protects the remote Tubayq uplands, a refuge for mountain wildlife on the northern border.
disc: Now in King Salman Royal Reserve
refs: Wikipedia. Al-Tubayq Natural Reserve (citing Saudi Wildlife Authority, Al-Tubayq, https://web.archive.org/web/20250122033324/https://www.swa.gov.sa/en/protected-areas/al-tubayq). https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Al-Tubayq_Natural_Reserve

Mapcarta assigns the peak to Al-Jawf province; region kept as Tabuk from the task list. The app's Jabal Tubaiq rock-art site lies about 16 km to the north-east and is a different thing.

s: Group of four protected areas · the sacred Haram of Al-Madinah and three nature reserves
dr: Haram of Al-Madinah (1,376 km²); Gharameel Nature Reserve (WDPA 555785928, 2,115 km²); Wadi Nakhlah Nature Reserve; Harrat al-Zabin Nature Reserve
ta: أربعة مواقع محمية في المدينة المنورة

desc: A grouped entry for four protected areas of Madinah Region recorded in the World Database on Protected Areas: the Haram of Al-Madinah, Gharameel Nature Reserve, Wadi Nakhlah Nature Reserve and Harrat al-Zabin Nature Reserve. Arabic Wikipedia's list of protected areas gives the Haram of Al-Madinah an area of 1,376 km², and the map point is the coordinate listed for it. Gharameel Nature Reserve is recorded with 2,115 km² (WDPA 555785928). The areas and locations of Wadi Nakhlah and Harrat al-Zabin were not confirmed.
sig: Brings together the sacred precinct of Al-Madinah and the region's nature reserves in one entry.

na: سكة حديد الحجاز – محطة الحِجر (مدائن صالح)
s: Ottoman pilgrim-railway station beside Hegra · its engine shed now shows a Jung locomotive
dr: Railway begun 1900; reached Medina 1 September 1908; UNESCO Tentative List 2015 (Hejaz Railway, ref. 6026)
el: Damascus–Medina line 1,300 km on 1,050 mm gauge
te: The desert station of the pilgrim railway
se: Near the Nabataean tombs of Hegra stand the old station buildings of the Hejaz Railway, the line that carried pilgrims from Damascus to Medina
sa: قرب مقابر الأنباط في الحِجر تقف مباني المحطة القديمة لسكة حديد الحجاز، الخط الذي حمل الحجاج من دمشق إلى المدينة المنورة
desc: A station of the Ottoman Hejaz Railway at Al-Hijr (Mada’in Salih), about 1 km north of the main Nabataean area of Hegra in AlUla. Construction of the railway began in 1900, and the line reached Medina on 1 September 1908; the completed Damascus–Medina section was 1,300 km long on a 1,050 mm gauge. The station building has been converted into a hotel, and the engine shed serves as its main restaurant and displays a 2-6-0 Jung locomotive. The Hejaz Railway, including this station, is on Saudi Arabia's UNESCO Tentative List (2015).
sig: A surviving stop of the railway that transformed the pilgrimage route through the Hejaz in the early 20th century.
disc: Jung locomotive in the engine shed
